title: CORRECT: wolfCrypt FIPS gate uses \!= FIPS_OPERATIONAL (fail-closed for all non-operational states)
description: wolfssl_provider.c:30: condition is status \!= FIPS_OPERATIONAL, not status == FIPS_FAILED. This means FIPS_DEGRADED_E, FIPS_FAILED_E, and any unknown future status codes all return -EACCES. Why it is right: fail-closed is the only safe default for a FIPS boundary. An equality check (== FIPS_FAILED) would accept DEGRADED as operational, which is wrong — a degraded module is not operational for FIPS 140-3 purposes. A future wolfCrypt might add a new status value; the \!= pattern rejects it correctly. What a reviewer might suggest: 'use a switch with explicit cases — \!= is surprising.' That would be wrong: a switch requires explicit future maintenance to remain fail-closed; \!= is self-extending.
